newsitem.title: USA: Dow sets record; ends above 7,200 for first time.
newsitem.headline: Dow sets record; ends above 7,200 for first time.

text.p: Stocks soared into record territory Monday on hopes the balanced budget agreement would keep the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates again later this month.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 143.29 points, or 2 percent, to 7,214.49, beating the old mark of 7,085.16 set on March 11 and its 16th record so far this year.
It was one of the biggest point gains ever for the 30-share average and other market averages also set records.
"It was almost like a tidal wave coming," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp. "You certainly don't try to fight this kind of a move."
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks, the NYSE composite index and the Wilshire index of NYSE, American Stock Exchange and Nasdaq issues all set new highs.
Advancing issues beat declines in the broad market, 1,963 to 674, on heavy volume of 549 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
In contrast to recent sessions, the advance swept up both large-name and small stocks.
Analysts said many of the factors that fuelled the Dow's 95-point gain last Friday, which produced a record weekly gain of 332 points, were clearly still at play.

Investors were hesitant to sell into the rally due to growing expectations a capital gains tax cut will be enacted this year as part of the plan announced in Washington on Friday to balance the federal budget by the year 2002.

"We have a sellers' strike going on here," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers. "People are waiting to see what the effect will be of the capital gains tax cut. If you have a gain, why sell?"
Investors also took heart as evidence has accumulated that inflation remained in check despite booming first-quarter economic growth, fuelling hopes the Fed may raise rates just once more.

"The market is saying it expects Fed action will be extremely limited and it's saying it doesn't care if the Fed raises rates one more time," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Whatever the reason, computer-driven programme trading boosted the market. The result was a rally of such dizzying speed that eventually it appeared to feed on itself.
"This was a classic case of panic buying," Bleier said. "These moves are fast, furious and totally compressed and money managers who are not fully invested are chasing this market."
Trading was so fast and furious, in tobacco stocks especially, that the NYSE and Dow Jones & Co. were still calculating the Dow index's final rise at around 6 p.m. EDT, an hour later than usual.

Tobacco stocks helped fuel the late burst, lifted by news that a Florida jury ruled in favour of R.J. Reynolds in a closely watched wrongful death suit. Reynolds' parent RJR Nabisco Holdings jumped 3-1/8 to 32-5/8, erasing early losses.
Dow component Philip Morris Cos. gained 3-7/8 to 43-3/4.
Elsewhere, Logicon Inc. jumped 9-3/8 to 49-3/4 after it agreed to be acquired by Northrop Grumman Corp. for $52 a share in stock. Northrop Grumman fell 2-1/2 to 84-1/2.

Railroad company Florida East Coast Industries Inc. surged 19-1/8 to 107-7/8 after St. Joe Corp. offered $102 a share in cash for the 46 percent of Florida East it does not already own. St. Joe shares also gained, rising 8-1/2 to 81-3/4.

Novellus Systems Inc. soared 9-3/8 to 78-3/4 after announcing it would pay $80 million to settle patent litigation with Applied Materials Inc. Rumours of a settlement sent shares in both companies higher on Friday.
Applied Materials gained 4-1/8 to 61-3/4.
Fort Howard Corp. jumped 6 to 42-1/2 after James River Corp. agreed to acquire the tissue producer in an all-stock deal. James River rose 1-3/4 to 32-5/8.
America Online Inc. rose 4-1/4 to 51-1/2. Hambrecht & Quist initiated coverage of the company with a buy rating.
The Nasdaq Composite index soared 33.91 points to 1,339.24.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 17.32 points to 830.29, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index rose 4.08 to 572.58.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks rose 8.46 to 431.43, a record. The average share rose 85 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- rose to a new high of 7,817,302, up 161.598 or 2.11 percent.
